releases.notes:
A safety check was reverting good updates.

After an update, ASCIA watches the system for a while and undoes the update if the appliance does
not come back healthy. That check was also treating "a supporting component is not the very newest
release available" as a failure — but ASCIA deliberately holds those components at versions it has
tested together, so that is the normal, intended state.

The result was that a perfectly healthy update could be undone for a reason undoing it could not
change. The check now looks only at things a rollback could actually fix.

Nothing about how your home behaves changes.
